solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carriage churning up one path

indicators.note: churning stirs the words one path about so their letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A carriage's wheels churn up a single path through the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churning up' signals an anagram of ONE PATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A phaeton is a light open four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Make more than one rise up — all possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the words rise up and all could be arranged some other way, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Someone urges a whole crowd to rise up and multiply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an anagram of RISE UP plus ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To pluralise a noun is to put it into the form meaning more than one, a grammatical term.

clue.text: Last two of these vats will be set up in the bars

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are turned so they read upwards
the final pair of letters of the word these is taken, here the letters S and E

parts.note: the word vats is taken as written; that the run also shows backwards across these vats is a coincidence of this device, not a separate hiding

explanation.surface: Instructions for a brewery: the last two vats are to be installed in the bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last two of' takes SE from 'these'; with VATS that makes SEVATS, and 'will be set up' reads it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Staves are wooden bars or poles, as also the strips forming a barrel.

clue.text: Statement about Bond's boss's bad behaviour

definitions.meaning: split one, two and five letters, the answer forms a sentence declaring that M, head of MI6, is in charge

explanation.walkthrough: M is James Bond's boss in the films and novels; the answer split 1,2,5 states his rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is playful naughtiness or troublesome conduct, so bad behaviour fits.

clue.text: Ordinary position for cat's-eyes?

definitions.meaning: literally the centre line of a highway, where reflective road studs are set

explanation.walkthrough: Cat's-eyes are reflective studs set into British roads, often along the centre line.
explanation.definitionFit: A moderate, unadventurous view or style is described with this idiom for steering a central course.

clue.text: Most keen to have a right nuisance quiet at the outset

parts.note: SH, the call for silence, which stands first in the answer
a pest is an annoying person or thing

explanation.surface: Someone very eager to have a thoroughly annoying person keep silent from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp means keen, as an edge or a mind, so the superlative gives most keen.

clue.text: Centre of planet with hydrogen rising to the top

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising to the top sends the chosen letter up to the first position

parts.note: Earth is our planet
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A science remark about the planet's core, with hydrogen floating upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising to the top' moves the H of EARTH to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its core or middle, a common synonym.

clue.text: Record one French priest as 'lover of good wine'?

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one
curé is the French word for a parish priest

explanation.surface: A French parish priest makes a recording and is labelled a wine enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person of refined taste in food and drink, so a connoisseur of fine wine is an example.

clue.text: Central heating allowed as protection for a house

parts.note: CH is the usual estate-agent abbreviation for central heating
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: An estate-agent listing: central heating permitted to protect the property.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a type of house, typically a wooden Alpine one.

clue.text: A twitching disorder follows small drink — it's striking

indicators.note: the twitch and the a come after the small drink in the answer

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone develops a nervous twitch after a nip of whisky, which is noticeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dramatic is vivid and arresting, which is what striking means.

clue.text: Being poor, obtained pence for pocketing

indicators.note: the word for obtained pockets, or holds inside it, the letter for pence

parts.note: derived means got or obtained from a source

explanation.surface: Someone poor has got hold of a few pennies to put in a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deprived is to lack basic necessities, i.e. to be poverty-stricken.

clue.text: Broadcast making one irritated

definitions.meaning: issued or transmitted, as a statement or programme

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to issue publicly and, as an adjective, annoyed.

clue.text: Come together, finding a form of solace in church

indicators.note: the rearranged solace sits inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the letters of solace are taken in a different form, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: People unite, finding comfort in their church.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to merge or unite into a single whole.

clue.text: I see old boy, someone on the tennis court?

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a server delivers the ball to start a tennis point

explanation.surface: Someone spots a former schoolmate playing tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' is playful: the answer could say it of itself, being one who sees.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer watches, so it is someone who could truthfully say they see.

clue.text: Once again putting an end to selling

definitions.text: Once again putting an end to
definitions.meaning: read as ..., giving something a tail, i.e. an end, again
the trade of selling goods to the public

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is semi-cryptic: the surface sense of halting is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailing is the sale of goods to the public, so it is a kind of selling.

clue.text: What could be wrongly represented as seediest UK region?

indicators.note: the letters of seediest are presented incorrectly, i.e. in another order

explanation.surface: A jibe at a British area as the seediest in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly represented' signals an anagram of SEEDIEST. Teesside is an area round the River Tees in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Teesside is an industrial area of north-east England, so it names a region of the UK.

clue.text: Concern for a financial premium

definitions.meaning: involvement or stake, as in a business concern
money paid on top of a loan or deposit

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a stake or concern in something and the extra charged for borrowing money.

clue.text: Out of the running these days, the woman with minimal energy

parts.note: now means at present
her refers to a woman
E, the abbreviation for energy, is just a single letter

explanation.surface: Nowadays a woman lacking energy can't compete.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing nowhere is an idiom for being unplaced in a race.

clue.text: Country embracing trade union law

indicators.note: the country word wraps its arms round the union letters

parts.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: A nation drawing a labour union into its legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Leaders of national party in cheerful female celebration

indicators.note: the two picked letters go inside the word for cheerful

parts.note: hearty means jovial and cheerful

indicators.note: the opening letters of national and party are taken

explanation.surface: Party leaders turn up at a jolly women's gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen party is a celebration for a bride-to-be and her female friends.

clue.text: Useless revolutionary academic full of sentimentality

indicators.note: the reversed academic is filled with the sentiment word
in a down entry, revolutionary turns the word round so it reads the other way

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
goo is mawkish sentimentality

explanation.surface: A pointless left-wing scholar brimming with sloppy sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no good is of no use, worthless.

clue.text: Saint suffering setback, getting feeble inside, twitches

indicators.note: the word for feeble goes within the reversed saint letters
a setback sends the saint letters backwards

parts.note: weak means feeble

explanation.surface: A holy man suffers a relapse, grows frail and starts twitching.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweaks as a noun are sharp pulls or twitches.

clue.text: Outside court a journalist functioned

indicators.note: the letters a and the journalist sit outside the court letters

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter worked outside a courthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to function or operate, so acted is functioned.

clue.text: Control report about good university

indicators.note: the report word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to relate is to report or recount

explanation.surface: Keeping a check on an account of a fine university.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate is to control or govern something by rules.

clue.text: Something very small and new leading to change of routine

indicators.note: the letter for new goes in front of what follows
a change of routine alters the order of its letters

explanation.surface: Something tiny and novel prompts a shake-up of habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' signals an anagram of ROUTINE, and 'leading to' puts N first.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is a subatomic particle with almost no mass, so it is minute.

clue.text: Fancy being overwhelmed by scorn at Eton!

indicators.note: the answer is swamped by, and so sits within, the words scorn at Eton

explanation.surface: Flamboyance meets disdain at the famous school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being overwhelmed by' shows the answer inside 'scorn at Eton'. Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means elaborate or highly decorated, a synonym.

clue.text: Decapitate dull principal!

parts.note: dead can mean dull or lifeless
the principal of a school is its head

explanation.surface: An order to behead a boring headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Gardeners use the word for removing spent flower heads.
explanation.definitionFit: To deadhead is to cut off withered flower heads, a literal beheading.
